Vulnérabilité critique CVE-2026-97668 (score CVSS 9.8).

The Abandoned Cart Pro for WooCommerce plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to SQL Injection via the guest cart persistent meta_value in all versions up to, and including, 10.8.0 due to insufficient escaping on user supplied data and lack of sufficient preparation on the existing SQL query in the update_guest_persistent_cart() function. The abandoned_cart_info value, populated from attacker-controlled checkout fields such as the SMS consent field, is passed through stripslashes() and concatenated directly into an UPDATE statement while the adjacent SELECT and INSERT use prepared statements. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to append additional SQL to the query. Because the sink is an UPDATE ... SET on the wp_usermeta table, the injection can both extract sensitive information from the database via time-based blind techniques and modify usermeta rows; it has been demonstrated to escalate an arbitrary account to administrator by writing a wp_capabilities row that shadows the legitimate one.

Vulnérabilité critique CVE-2026-97657 (score CVSS 9.8).

The Abandoned Cart Pro for WooCommerce plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Authentication Bypass via Malleable Encryption and Bypassable HMAC in all versions up to, and including, 10.8.0. This is due to the use of MAC-free AES-CTR encryption for cart-recovery link tokens — where the 8-byte CTR nonce is carried inside the ciphertext blob and the encryption key is looked up using the attacker-supplied `user_email` GET parameter — combined with an HMAC nonce check in `wcap_email_track_links()` that is only enforced when the `wcap_nonce` parameter is non-empty, allowing complete bypass by omission, and an insecure direct object reference on the decrypted `abandoned_id` with no ownership verification confirming the cart belongs to the email used for decryption. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers who possess a single legitimate cart-recovery link (obtained from their own reminder email) to recover the keystream, forge a ciphertext that decrypts to any victim's cart ID, and trigger a call to `wp_set_auth_cookie()` for the victim user — achieving full account takeover of any user who has ever abandoned a cart, including administrators. The auto-login feature defaults to enabled and is forced on during plugin upgrades, meaning all affected installations are exploitable without any additional configuration.

Score CVSS : 9.8

Type de faiblesse (CWE) : CWE-639

This is due to missing WordPress bootstrap, authentication, capability, and nonce checks in the standalone save-to-cache.php script, combined with insufficient sanitization of the pluginURL parameter before it is written to a web-executable PHP file. items.detail:
Incident de sécurité rapporté par The Record.

An Ohio-based company charged individuals thousands of dollars to fight sextortion scams, but the operation itself was fraudulent, according to a Federal Trade Commission complaint.

Digital Forensics Corporation (DFC), owner Dmitry Belkin and several affiliated companies are behind the scheme, which allegedly ran from February 2023 through July 2026, the FTC said. A federal court has temporarily ordered the “sextortion assistance” company from doing business until a decision is reached, the agency said.

Desperate defendants receiving threats from sextortionists who said they will share naked photos or other sensitive sexual information with family members and employers have turned to DFC for help only to be manipulated into spending thousands, the FTC said in a press release .

In reality, DFC did none of these things, according to the FTC.

“Instead of communicating with the sextortionist through the victim's account, defendants routinely change the victim's account settings simply to block the sextortionist's communications,” the complaint said. “Instead of obtaining investigative information, defendants fabricate chat transcripts.”

DFC also allegedly routinely reused pre-saved location coordinates — typically for Nigeria and the Philippines — to trick customers into believing they had located the sextortionist.

The company used a script for sales calls, the complaint said, and would customize language to play to specific fears different victims might have. For example, victims in the military would be told they could face a dishonorable discharge while married victims were warned that a sextortionist could target their spouses and in-laws, the complaint said.

Signal de veille — The Record.

More than 40 residences in Texas were the target of a federal operation in September to clamp down on remote worker scams that feed money back to the North Korean regime.

The Department of Justice disrupted multiple laptop farms across Texas allegedly being used by North Korean nationals to facilitate an IT worker scheme that allows the country to earn millions from U.S. companies.

The laptop farm raids, which were conducted September 21-25, targeted more than 40 residences, the DOJ said.

Law enforcement seized 187 laptops and other devices used by North Koreans. Such schemes have earned millions over the last eight years by tricking U.S. companies into hiring workers remotely into lucrative IT roles through stolen or purchased identities.

Alongside the raids, the DOJ indicted and arrested U.S. nationals Michael James Bostelle of Pennsylvania and Juan Cecilio Pena Carrillo of Texas. Several Chinese and North Korean nationals also were indicted. The department did not respond to requests for comment about whether the indictments and arrests were linked to the Texas laptop farm raids.

The DOJ indicted Bostelle and Pena on wire fraud, money laundering, and identity theft charges, accusing them of being key U.S.-based cogs in the IT worker scheme.

Large parts of the indictment are centered around U.S. national Trey Michael Nolte, who was not charged.

Signal de veille — The Record.

More than two dozen people were arrested by police in Ghana and Nigeria as part of a U.K.-hosted operation that also included tech companies.

Police in Ghana and Nigeria arrested or detained 28 people and identified more than 100 suspected victims of human trafficking during an international operation targeting scam compounds in West Africa, U.S. and British officials announced Tuesday.

The operation was hosted by Britain’s National Crime Agency (NCA) in London last week. It brought together 15 law enforcement agencies and the same number of tech companies — including Meta, Microsoft and Google — as part of what they called Joint Disruption Week.

In Ghana, authorities raided a compound in Sasaabi, a semi-rural community outside the capital, Accra, arresting 19 people and seizing 303 devices, according to the U.S. Department of Justice. Nigerian authorities made nine further arrests.

“These networks steal savings on one side of the screen, and people’s freedom on the other,” said Matthew Floyd, a deputy assistant director in the FBI’s Criminal Division.

The Department of Justice said the technology companies it worked with removed more than 3.7 million accounts, pages and groups linked to the West African scam centres.

Meta’s Rob Cochrane gave the same figure for Facebook and Instagram alone. The department did not break the total down by company.

While three quarters of security teams have yet to fully investigate the potential deployment of AI tools into their security operations, 20% of those surveyed said that they are running a closed pilot scheme, and a further 35% said they are examining the potential of adoption within the next 12 to 24 months. Of those who are using or are piloting AI agents, tasks these tools are involved in include information retrieval and alert prioritization, as well as more active tasks such as blocking IP addresses, updating blacklists and monitoring suspicious traffic.
